"Biology has been just sort of a clever discovery-based science until this point," Chan said in an interview. "We have always held this as a community asset, not just for one group, so that it can build upon itself over time.”  The datasets will eventually be released publicly, but companies that fund them get a head start, according to Biohub's head of science Alex Rives. "With commercial funders we have embargo periods where there's a period of time where the groups can work on the data, and then it becomes available as a public scientific resource," Rives said.  The arrangement is how Biohub is drawing private money into a project it describes as open science. Rives said the government-funded work running in parallel will carry no such restrictions, and that Biohub plans to approach pharmaceutical companies and philanthropies next. Current cell datasets run to hundreds of millions of cells, Rives said, while an accurate predictive model will require billions and eventually trillions. Biohub's goal is to close that gap. "We need to capture the language of biology, we need to capture the language of the cell. And that doesn't exist today," he said. The data will come from techniques including spatial transcriptomics, which maps molecular activity inside intact tissue, and screens that record how cells respond to changes in environment. Much of it has never been generated in a coordinated way. Rives said the work would normally take decades and that the partners aim to compress it into five years, with a first dataset ready in about a year. He expects accurate predictive models within five years. Other AI labs are pursuing similar initiatives. Anthropic doubled down on its biology efforts with a wet lab, while the OpenAI Foundation started a more than $125 million grant program to fund biological and medical datasets for AI research.

Source: Reuters

item.title: Euro cae hacia mínimos de 17 meses, dólar mantiene ganancias tras minutas Fed
item.description: El euro cayó el miércoles, ya que los bonos franceses sufrieron nuevas presiones por preocupaciones fiscales, mientras el dólar mantuvo sus ganancias tras la publicación de las minutas de la última cita de la Reserva Federal.
item.dc:creator: Chuck Mikolajczak
item.content:encoded: El euro cayó el miércoles, ya que los bonos franceses sufrieron nuevas presiones por preocupaciones fiscales, mientras el dólar mantuvo sus ganancias tras la publicación de las minutas de la última cita de la Reserva Federal. * El retorno de los bonos de Francia y España aumentó y el de los países más endeudados registró un alza más pronunciada que el de activos de refugio como los alemanes, a medida que persisten las preocupaciones fiscales en Francia y los precios del crudo retoman protagonismo. * El rendimiento del bono francés a 10 años se disparó 11,9 puntos básicos, en su mayor aumento diario en dos semanas, al 4,8696%, mientras que el de su par alemán se mantuvo sin cambios en el 3,4805%. * "Lo que ocurre en Europa es que, durante un tiempo, han funcionado un poco al estilo del Estado del bienestar, gastando mucho dinero sin generar realmente muchos ingresos, y eso finalmente les está pasando factura", dijo Juan Pérez, de Monex USA en Washington. * "Si a esto le sumamos que todo el mundo ha tenido que gastar más dinero en energía, las perspectivas no son buenas. La atención se centra en Europa, y el panorama es muy, muy negativo", agregó. * El euro perdió un 0,53%, a 1,1198 dólares, cerca de los mínimos de 17 meses registrados el lunes. * El índice dólar , que compara al billete verde con una cesta de seis destacadas divisas, ganó un 0,32%, a 102,24 unidades; tras recortar brevemente sus ganancias, volvió a repuntar después de conocerse las minutas de la Fed. * Las actas revelaron que los responsables de política monetaria estaban divididos el mes pasado sobre los motivos para subir las tasas. "Algunos participantes" consideraban necesaria un alza para contener el impacto de los choques en los precios de la energía y otros bienes, mientras que un grupo más partidario de una política restrictiva la veía necesaria para prevenir una inflación emergente impulsada por la demanda. * El dólar también se vio respaldado por la persistencia de unos precios energéticos elevados, si bien el petróleo perdió las ganancias iniciales en una sesión volátil, después de que la Agencia Internacional de la Energía acordara acelerar la liberación de reservas de crudo y priorizar el diésel para combatir los precios récord del combustible. * Mientras, la libra esterlina restó un 0,42%, a 1,3216 dólares, pero alcanzó su nivel más alto desde junio de 2025 ante el euro. Frente al yen , el dólar cedió un 0,09%, a 157,95 unidades.

FAST

Oct 7 : Global stocks and the euro pulled back on Wednesday as oil prices held near $100 amid renewed Middle East tensions while concerns France's fiscal woes could affect broader debt markets continued to weigh on overall sentiment. The S&P 500 slid 0.3 per cent a day after it hit a new record. The tech-heavy Nasdaq fell 0.4 per cent, also pulling back from a fresh all-time high. MSCI's main world stocks index fell 0.6 per cent, while Europe's STOXX 600 was down 1 per cent, near its lowest level since June. “In the very early stages of the fourth quarter, typically the best quarter of the year for equity returns, markets are being driven by a confusing ‘stocks up, US breadth down, yields up, oil down and up, and down...’ narrative,” said Jeremy Batstone-Carr, an economist at Raymond James.

Brent crude lingered around $100 per barrel as the market weighed supply constraints from a storm heading for US oil-producing regions and attacks by Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis on Saudi Arabia. US crude dipped 0.9 per cent to $88.63 a barrel. Aneeka Gupta, director of research at WisdomTree, credited still "really strong" earnings expectations for the stock market's relative resilience in the face of rallying oil prices. "That's what's really holding up the market so far," Gupta said. The French yield spread against safe-haven German Bunds — a market gauge of the risk premium investors demand to hold French debt — was about 11 basis points (bps) wider after narrowing for two days. It was last trading near 140 bps, and reached almost 160 bps last week. French bonds have been under pressure as expectations of higher European Central Bank rates and political uncertainty before the 2027 election raise doubts over France's ability to fix its finances. EURO DOWN ON RATE DIVERGENCE, FISCAL CONCERNS The rekindling of investor concerns weighed on the euro, which slipped 0.6 per cent to $1.119. It slid to a 17-month low against the dollar at $1.1161 earlier this week. Wider yield spreads in the euro area weigh on the single currency by boosting expectations of ECB monetary easing, reviving worries about fiscal sustainability and stoking fears of increasing fragmentation in the euro area. Markets also closely watched the rate divergence between the US and the euro area as they priced in a more hawkish Federal Reserve after the mid-September policy meeting. "The interest rate spread between Germany and the US became more negative, which provided support to the US dollar against the euro," Georgette Boele, senior currency and oil strategist at ABN AMRO, said. "We continue to believe that financial markets are pricing in too many rate increases by the Fed and the ECB," she said. US TREASURY AUCTIONS, FED MINUTES IN FOCUS The yield on benchmark U.S. 10-year notes rose 1.91 basis points to 5.29 per cent  Market participants will closely watch a 10-year Treasury auction later in the day and a 30-year auction on Thursday, which will show the depth of investor demand for US debt, analysts said. US longer-dated yields hit a 24-year high on Monday amid a persistent selloff since late August due to concerns over inflation and the fiscal outlook. The dollar index, which measures its performance against a basket of currencies, rose about 0.4 per cent, following a 0.27 per cent slide in the prior session.  The Federal Reserve on Wednesday will publish the minutes of its September 15 to 16 policy meeting, which will be scrutinised for clues about potential rate moves over the next few months. Traders cut the odds of a Fed rate hike in October to 19 per cent from about 50 per cent a week earlier.

Source: Reuters

item.title: France suspends use of stun grenades to police student protests
item.description: The French government said on Wednesday it was pausing the use of stun grenades in its policing of student protests, after a 15-year-old boy's hand was blown off during a clash with riot police, fuelling protesters' accusations of police brutality.
item.dc:creator: Makini Brice, Janis Laizans
item.content:encoded: The French government said on Wednesday it was pausing the use of stun grenades in its policing of [USN:L1N45S0C7 TEXT:"student protests"], after a 15-year-old boy's [USN:L1N45R08Q TEXT:"hand was blown off"] during a clash with riot police, fuelling protesters' accusations of police brutality. Protests showed no sign of easing, with more than 500 schools closed a day after demonstrations swept across the country, and unions representing high-school students, teachers and other workers planning more marches for Thursday. The wave of protests has been going on for more than two weeks and has exposed widespread public anger six months ahead of an election to replace President Emmanuel Macron. Speaking to the nation on Wednesday evening, Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu said the government would review the demands made by students and present proposals at the end of October on issues ranging from renovating buildings to make more teachers available, but gave no details. "In the past, too many promises were not kept, quite simply because they were untenable," Lecornu said. "What I want are concrete, quick and fully funded answers." The lack of an immediate government response, which was decried by student leaders after talks at the education ministry earlier on Wednesday, appeared unlikely to quell the protests. At Lycee Lamartine, a high school in central Paris, protesters sang the Marseillaise, chanted slogans and performed Mexican waves as they blockaded the entrance to the school. "We saw there were lots of crumbling walls, a shortage of teachers in public schools, absent teachers," said Gabriel Fillieule, who used to attend a public school but now goes to a private one. He and others said they were protesting to demand better learning conditions for all. POLICE'S USE OF FORCE BEING INVESTIGATED While most of Wednesday's blockades were peaceful, police used tear gas and pushed back protesters in a street barricaded by rubbish bins outside Sciences Po university in central Paris. Rights groups, labour unions, students and some opposition politicians have accused the police of using disproportionate force to quell the wave of protests. Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said he had ordered the suspension of the use of stun grenades following an incident in the northern city of Lens on Monday in which there was a "strong possibility" the firing of a stun grenade had caused a teenager to lose his hand. "I am suspending their use for the high-school students' movement until light has been shed on what happened in this case," said the minister, who added that 18 incidents in total had been referred to the police inspectorate for investigation. Protesters have said they blame poor learning conditions for a sharp drop in French teenagers' scores in reading and maths over the past decade. French 15-year-olds scored 43 points lower in reading in 2025 than in 2015, according to the OECD's Programme for International Student Assessment, the biggest drop among the OECD countries. Their maths scores also dropped the most. But the government, under pressure to tame public debt amid weak growth, has little spare cash to address students' complaints of teacher shortages, ageing school buildings and inequalities between schools in affluent and poor areas. TWENTY-FOUR HIGH SCHOOLS DAMAGED BY FIRE OR VANDALISM Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu has acknowledged the "legitimate" demands of France's students but also described the unrest as the most violent student demonstrations in decades. Education Minister Edouard Geffray told parliament that 24 high schools had been damaged by fire or vandalism to the extent that they would remain closed for weeks, meaning some 30,000 students would receive no in-person teaching until they reopened. He estimated it would cost €20 million to €30 million ($22 million to $34 million) to fix the damage. Far-right presidential candidate Marine Le Pen, the frontrunner according to opinion polls, said those who damaged schools should pay for the repairs rather than taxpayers. The government has adopted a similar stance and has a bill going through parliament that aims to set up such a system. According to an Elabe poll for BFM TV, 72% of French people think the students' demands are legitimate, but 55% of them think the protests should stop. UNREST ELSEWHERE Elsewhere in Europe, where budgets have been under pressure as governments respond to successive cost-of-living and energy crises, students in parts of Belgium staged similar protests. In the Belgian city of Liege in the southern French-speaking Wallonia region, at least 107 people have been arrested in connection with student protests this month, the Belga news agency reported. Teachers are also on strike. In Portugal, the main teachers' union FENPROF launched an indefinite strike in mid-September over working conditions, with teachers refusing to do any unpaid work beyond the 35 hours a week mandated by law. And in Spain, teachers' unions have been protesting conditions in state schools. Teachers in Madrid plan a strike on October 14 to press demands including a reduction in hours, smaller class sizes and higher salaries. ($1 = 0.8952 euros)

item.title: Five more UK rate-rigging convictions quashed as SFO prosecutions unravel
item.description: Five former Barclays traders, jailed in Britain for plotting to rig global benchmark interest rates, won an appeal to clear their names on Wednesday, further unravelling some of the UK Serious Fraud Office's most high-profile prosecutions.
item.dc:creator: Kirstin Ridley
item.content:encoded: Five former Barclays (BARC.L) traders, jailed in Britain for plotting to rig global benchmark interest rates, won an appeal to clear their names on Wednesday, further unravelling some of the UK Serious Fraud Office's most high-profile prosecutions. London's Court of Appeal quashed the [USN:L8N3YU25P TEXT:"convictions"] of Philippe Moryoussef, from France, Kolkata-born Jay Merchant, Britons Colin Bermingham and Jonathan Mathew, and Alex Pabon, an American. The traders were cast by prosecutors as a symbol of banker greed at a time of taxpayer fury at eye-watering bank bailouts following the 2007-2009 credit crisis, which sent stock markets plunging and pitched economies into recession. But the men applied to clear their names after the Supreme Court last year [USN:L8N3TK0IL TEXT:"overturned"] the convictions of [USN:L1N3W9013 TEXT:"Tom Hayes"] — a former star UBS (UBSG.S) and Citigroup (C.N) trader — and ex-Barclays peer Carlo Palombo for rigging now-defunct interbank interest rate Libor and its euro equivalent, Euribor. The Supreme Court ruled that the trial judges had misdirected juries and that legal errors undermined the fairness of the trials, laying the groundwork for Wednesday's appeals. "All five convictions were rendered unsafe by the same series of errors ... For those reasons, all five convictions will be quashed," the Court of Appeal said. TEARFUL TRADER SAYS DECISION HARD TO TAKE IN Merchant, Pabon, Moryoussef, Bermingham and Mathew were convicted of conspiracy to defraud and sentenced to between 33 months and 8 years in jail between 2016 and 2019 after a series of landmark SFO trials. "It's hard to take in," said a tearful Bermingham, 70, outside the courtroom. "You don't believe it until you hear it." Moryoussef, now 58, gained notoriety for jumping bail and fleeing to France. He was tried in London in his absence, sentenced to eight years and has remained a fugitive since. "Today, I am regaining my soul, and for the first time, I can envision my next chapter in peace," he said in a statement. Pabon, 48, noted: "Ten years ago, my jury was told, as a matter of law, that an honest answer to the Libor question was not a defence. The Serious Fraud Office now accepts my conviction is unsafe." The SFO reiterated that the Supreme Court had found "ample evidence" on which a properly directed jury could have convicted Hayes and Palombo. But it added: "After carefully considering this judgment and the full circumstances, we do not oppose the appeals of five individuals convicted by juries in relation to Libor and Euribor." A further attempted appeal by Christian Bittar, a French former Deutsche Bank (DBKGn.DE) trader sentenced to jail in 2018, is expected to be heard on Friday. Bittar, once dubbed one of the world's most skilled traders, is the only appellant whose case is being contested by the SFO following his guilty plea more than eight years ago. Designed to estimate the costs at which banks would lend to each other, Libor and Euribor were once a benchmark for interest rates underpinning around $450 trillion of financial contracts, from derivatives to student loans.

item.title: Barril cae tras acuerdo de la AIE de acelerar la liberación de reservas
item.description: Los precios del petróleo cayeron el miércoles, después de que la Agencia Internacional de la Energía acordara acelerar la liberación de reservas y dar prioridad al gasóleo, en un intento por frenar los precios récord de los combustibles, mientras la guerra en Irán reduce el suministro mundial.
item.dc:creator: Georgina Mccartney
item.content:encoded: Los precios del petróleo cayeron el miércoles, después de que la Agencia Internacional de la Energía acordara acelerar la liberación de reservas y dar prioridad al gasóleo, en un intento por frenar los precios récord de los combustibles, mientras la guerra en Irán reduce el suministro mundial. * Los futuros del Brent bajaban 0,5 dólares, o un 0,5%, a 100,08 dólares por barril, mientras que el West Texas Intermediate en Estados Unidos (WTI) caía 1,18 dólares, o un 1,32%, a 88,26 dólares. * La AIE señaló que llevar a cabo lo antes posible las liberaciones anunciadas anteriormente podría aportar unos 100 millones de barriles al mercado, aunque analistas y algunos gobiernos indicaron que esa cifra no representaba necesariamente una nueva intervención de tal magnitud. * Francia liberará 10 millones de barriles de gasóleo de sus reservas estratégicas, informó el miércoles la emisora Franceinfo, citando fuentes anónimas. * "Europa es el epicentro de toda esta crisis de suministro (...) y estas liberaciones abordan ese problema y alivian en cierta medida la presión sobre la demanda de WTI. Esto debería reducir parte de la presión sobre los suministros estadounidenses", afirmó John Kilduff, socio de Again Capital. * Las reservas de crudo en Estados Unidos cayeron en 3,2 millones de barriles a 424,1 millones de barriles en la semana que finalizó el 2 de octubre, según la Administración de Información de Energía (EIA), frente a las previsiones de los analistas en una encuesta de Reuters, que apuntaban a un aumento de 1,7 millones de barriles. * Según Tamas Varga, analista de PVM, los inversores no están convencidos de que los recientes aumentos de la oferta y las exportaciones procedentes de Oriente Medio sean sostenibles. * La presión a la baja sobre los precios remitió debido a la proximidad de la tormenta en Estados Unidos, así como a los conflictos en Oriente Medio y Ucrania, señaló Varga. * Los hutíes de Yemen atacaron el miércoles el aeropuerto internacional de Adén con misiles balísticos y drones cargados de explosivos, según informó el Ministerio de Transporte del país, mientras se intensifican los combates entre el grupo alineado con Irán y las fuerzas gubernamentales respaldadas por Arabia Saudita. * Ucrania atacó el miércoles dos instalaciones petroleras rusas, mientras que Rusia bombardeó Ucrania con oleadas de misiles y drones, lo que provocó la muerte de al menos 15 personas, según informaron las autoridades ucranianas. * Los ataques contra la infraestructura energética rusa y la pérdida de capacidad de refino en Oriente Medio han tensado los mercados de combustible, afirmó el martes el presidente ejecutivo de Vitol, Russell Hardy. * En Estados Unidos, meteorólogos afirmaron el martes que una tormenta que se está formando en el golfo de México se convertirá en el primer huracán del Atlántico de 2026 en un plazo de dos días. Las zonas marítimas situadas en la trayectoria de la tormenta producen el 15% del crudo estadounidense y el 5% del gas natural del país.

item.title: Life sciences firm Danaher to launch AI-powered autonomous research lab in 2027
item.description: Life sciences company Danaher said on Wednesday it plans to launch its first AI-powered autonomous research lab early next year to make drug discovery and development faster and more efficient.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Life sciences company Danaher (DHR.N) said on Wednesday it plans to launch its first AI-powered autonomous research lab early next year to make drug discovery and development faster and more efficient. Here are more details: The lab, projected to operate at scale in early 2027, will combine AI, robotics and technologies from several Danaher operating companies in one connected workflow to develop custom antibodies and other molecular tools It is expected to make discovering molecules eight times faster and unlock a tenfold increase in generating target-binding molecules annually "That frees them (scientists) to focus on the complex scientific challenges where human insight matters most," said JC Gutierrez-Ramos, chief science officer of Danaher The lab uses AI to help create new molecules that can bind specifically to a biological target, including antibodies, then builds and tests each one, feeding every result back into the model to improve the next design The lab is an example of a broader program across Danaher, intended to create a fleet of smart instruments, the company said

[７日 ロイター] - 米抵当銀行協会（ＭＢＡ）が７日発表した３０年固定住宅ローンの週平均金利（２日までの週）は７．４９％で、前週から１９ベーシスポイント（ｂｐ）上昇し、約３年ぶりの高水準となった。

先週の住宅ローン申請は前週比４．２％減。借り換え申請が大幅に減少したという。

ＭＢＡの副チーフエコノミスト、ジョエル・カン氏は「現在の金利水準では、借り換えを検討する住宅所有者はごく少数であり、借入コストの上昇により、多くの潜在的な借り手が住宅購入市場から離れている」と述べた。

item.title: US 30-year mortgage rate hits highest in nearly three years
item.description: The interest rate on the most common US home loan jumped last week to its highest in almost three years, worsening affordability for buyers four weeks before elections that will decide if President Donald Trump's Republicans keep control of Congress.
item.dc:creator: Ann Saphir
item.content:encoded: The interest rate on the most common US home loan jumped last week to its highest in almost three years, worsening affordability for buyers four weeks before elections that will decide if President Donald Trump's Republicans keep control of Congress. The average 30-year fixed-rate mortgage surged 19 basis points to 7.49% in the week ended October 2, the Mortgage Bankers Association said on Wednesday. It was last higher in November 2023. Mortgage rates are tied closely to the yield on US 10-year Treasury notes, which earlier this week [USN:L8N45T0F3 TEXT:"hit a 24-year high"], driven by worries over inflationary pressures from soaring oil prices and data showing stronger US economic growth. The cost of living is the top issue on Americans' minds as they decide how they will vote on November 3, a Reuters/Ipsos poll completed on Monday showed, and is one reason why Trump's [USN:L6N45R10Y TEXT:"approval rating"] is at a record low of 32%. Home borrowing rates are up about 1.4 percentage points since joint US-Israeli strikes against Iran began in late February, tracking a similar rise in the 10-year Treasury yield, which topped 5.3% on Monday. Inflation is also on the rise, registering 3.4% in August by a measure that the Federal Reserve targets at 2%. Fed policymakers have signaled they expect to follow their September interest-rate increase with another rate hike by year's end, though markets are for now betting they will not move at their upcoming policy meeting at the end of October. Asked by a reporter Wednesday about mortgage rates, Trump called Fed chairman Kevin Warsh "great," but added the rest of the board "would like to see the country do badly, in my opinion, because I think interest rates should come down." US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, in the Oval Office with Trump, blamed inflation and high mortgage rates on the temporary shock from higher oil prices. "So once we get on the other side of this Iran conflict, (the) energy market is going to be well supplied, and we will move down towards the Fed's target and mortgage rates and the 10-year will come back down," Bessent said. Mortgage loan applications fell 4.2% last week from the previous week, the MBA said on Wednesday, with refinancing applications dropping sharply. Overall application volumes are the lowest since February 2025 and have fallen nearly 50% since January. "Very few homeowners have an incentive to refinance at these rates, and the jump in borrowing costs has caused many potential borrowers to step back from the purchase market," said Joel Kan, the MBA’s deputy chief economist.

item.title: UPS to hire 100,000 temporary workers for holiday season
item.description: United Parcel Service on Wednesday said it would hire 100,000 seasonal employees across the US, as it prepares for a spike in parcel volumes for the upcoming holiday season.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: United Parcel Service (UPS.N) on Wednesday said it would hire 100,000 seasonal employees across the US, as it prepares for a spike in parcel volumes for the upcoming holiday season. Here are some details: The holiday season is the busiest period for parcel delivery companies, during which daily volumes tend to double. Shippers and most retailers boost the hiring of temporary workers during the period from late November to early January. The seasonal workers will help sort, move and deliver packages during the holiday rush, UPS said. The parcel delivery company hired 125,000 holiday season staff in 2024, but did not provide a comparable hiring number last year. In January, the company said it would cut [USN:L4N3YS10F TEXT:"up to 30,000 operational jobs"] and close 24 facilities in 2026 in a bid to scale down shipments for its largest customer, Amazon, and shift towards more profitable shipments.

item.title: ロシア当局「ペスト流行リスクなし」、研究職員死亡巡りメディア批判
item.description:
Andrew Osborn Jennifer Rigby
［モスクワ／ロンドン ７日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Andrew Osborn　Jennifer Rigby

［モスクワ／ロンドン　７日　ロイター］ - ロシアの衛生当局は７日、東部シベリアのペスト研究所の職員が死亡した事例について、同地域で流行が広がるリスクはないと表明した。一方、世界保健機関（ＷＨＯ）はロシア政府に対し、死因に関するさらなる情報の提供を求めている。

シベリア地方のイルクーツク州にある研究所の女性職員（２８）が２日、原因不明の肺炎で死亡した。この事例を巡っては、トランプ米大統領を含め国際的な懸念が広がり、当初は約２００人が隔離対象となった。

ロシアの衛生監視機関である消費者権利保護・福祉監督庁（ロスポトレブナゾール）は声明で、流行のリスクはないと結論付けたとして予防措置を縮小しつつあると表明。ＷＨＯとも最新情報を共有したとした。死亡した職員と接触した人の中からペストの症例は確認されておらず、約５０００件の検査でも危険な病原体は検出されなかったため、隔離対象者の９０％が解除されたという。

また、同職員はワクチン接種を受けており、「業務で扱っていた危険な感染症に対する免疫を獲得していた」とした。ただし、死因となった肺炎の原因や感染経路については明らかにしなかった。

＜大統領府、メディアの「虚偽情報」を批判＞

ロシア大統領府のペスコフ報道官は、所定の手続きに従って事件についてＷＨＯに適切に報告したと述べた。メディア報道を事態の根拠として用いることに慎重であるべきだとした上で、「報道は非常に多いが、メディアがこの件について伝えていることの大半は虚偽の情報だ」と批判した。

ペスコフ氏はメディアなどに対し、衛生当局の発表する情報に依拠するよう助言した。

米ＡＢＣニュースはこれに先立ち、「米国がこの死亡事例へのロシアの対応について正式な外交抗議を申し入れ、ロシアに対し同事例に関する透明性の向上を求めた」と報じていた。

ペスコフ氏はまた、現時点ではプーチン大統領とトランプ米大統領との間で電話会談の予定は入っていないと述べた。トランプ氏は６日、この件について「まもなく」プーチン氏と話し合うと述べていた。

item.title: 独、テスラの運転支援システムのＥＵ承認を推進 マスク氏が歓迎
item.description:
Marie Mannes Miranda Murray
[ベルリン ７日 ロイター] - 米電気自動車（ＥＶ）大手テス...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
独、テスラの運転支援システムのＥＵ承認を推進　マスク氏が歓迎 10/7 19:43 配信

資料写真：2026年4月14日、中国・上海で行われた政府主催のメディアツアーの際に、テスラ・ギガファクトリーに掲げられたテスラのロゴ。 REUTERS/Go Nakamura/File Photo

Marie Mannes　Miranda Murray

[ベルリン ７日 ロイター] - 米電気自動車（ＥＶ）大手テスラのイーロン・マスク最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）は７日、同社の運転支援システム「フルセルフドライビング」に対するドイツ政府の支持を歓迎した。同氏は、交通安全の専門家らが「安全性の主張が誇張されている」と警告する「フルセルフドライビング」について、欧州全域での承認を目指している。

マスク氏は、ドイツのビルガー交通相が欧州全域での「フルセルフドライビング」の承認を推進していることを受け、Ｘにドイツ語で「ありがとう」と投稿した。

ビルガー氏は６日の声明で、先月にテスラと数多くの技術的詳細や責任問題について協議した結果、「フルセルフドライビング」のＥＵによる迅速な承認を提唱していると述べた。

協議の一環で、ドイツはテスラと、「フルセルフドライビング」で制限速度を最大１０％まで超過してもよいことで合意した。速度超過が主な争点の一つとなっている欧州の承認プロセスにおいても、ドイツはこのアプローチを支持する方針だ。

一方、交通安全の専門家や一部の規制当局は、テスラが採用している「速度オフセット機能」（システムが制限速度を超えて走行することを可能にする機能）は、欧州での承認前に削除されるべきだと主張している。

ビルガー氏はまた、システム名が多少誤解を招くという懸念に対処するため、テスラがシステム名を「テスラ・アシスト・ドライビング」に変更することを提案したと明らかにした。同システムは運転を支援するものではあるが、完全な自動運転ではない。

フルセルフドライビングはすでにオランダやベルギーなど欧州の一部で認可されている。

しかし、スウェーデンやフランスを含むいくつかのＥＵ加盟国は、同システムが制限速度を超えることへの懸念を表明しており、１０月に予定されていたＥＵの採決は、一部の国が追加試験を行う間、少なくとも１２月まで延期された。

item.title: Wall Street ends lower, off record highs, as Treasury yields climb
item.description: Wall Street closed lower on Wednesday, as long-dated US Treasury yields resumed their climb, reviving fears about inflation and mounting debt the day after the S&P 500 and the Nasdaq hit record closing highs.
item.dc:creator: Stephen Culp, Tharuniyaa Lakshmi
item.content:encoded: Wall Street closed lower on Wednesday, as long-dated US Treasury yields resumed their climb, reviving fears about inflation and mounting debt the day after the S&P 500 and the Nasdaq hit record closing highs. All three major US stock indexes were modestly lower, with the S&P 500 and the Dow snapping four-day winning streaks. The Nasdaq notched its first down day in six. The small-cap Russell 2000 (.RUT) underperformed its larger cap counterparts, dropping 1.3%. In the wake of Tuesday's stock market rally, Brent crude settled above $100 per barrel and long-dated Treasury yields touched a [USN:L8N45T0F3 TEXT:"24-year high"]. Iran war-related [USN:L1N45T02U TEXT:"supply concerns"] have led to soaring oil prices, which in turn have revived inflation worries and raised the chances of a prolonged central bank rate hiking cycle. Those concerns, combined with mounting corporate and sovereign debt levels, have caused a global bond selloff, which rattled global markets in recent weeks. Investors "have been looking for some relief on oil, which would drive some relief on rates and that would therefore help the stock market," said Thomas Martin, senior portfolio manager at GLOBALT in Atlanta. "The third quarter was supposed to be the weak quarter of the year; we were supposed to get a correction," Martin added. "That didn't happen, so it's three cheers and let's take some money off the table." Stocks pared losses after [USN:L1N45T02U TEXT:"crude prices"] turned lower following the International Energy Agency's agreement to speed up the release of oil stocks, prioritizing diesel. [USN:L6N45T0TQ TEXT:"Minutes"] from the US Federal Reserve's September monetary policy meeting, at which the central bank unanimously approved its first interest rate hike since July 2023, revealed divisions over the rationale of the increase. Some participants saw a hike as necessary to keep the impact of energy price shocks at bay, while others felt the increase was necessary to curb demand-driven inflation. Financial markets are currently pricing in a 17.2% likelihood that the Fed will implement a second consecutive rate hike at the conclusion of its October meeting, down from 37.6% a week ago, per CME's FedWatch tool. "The market’s Fed expectations are going to seesaw as it gets new bits of data," Martin said. "There's still an expectation for more rate hikes, but it isn't necessarily going to be a hike every meeting and that's what the market is telling you; October will be a pause." The Dow Jones Industrial Average (.DJI) fell 341.11 points, or 0.66%, to 51,180.17, the S&P 500 (.SPX) lost 17.18 points, or 0.22%, to 7,801.75 and the Nasdaq Composite (.IXIC) lost 61.19 points, or 0.22%, to 27,538.69. Among the 11 sectors in the S&P 500, industrials (.SPLRCI) suffered the steepest percentage drop, while healthcare stocks (.SPXHC) led the gainers. Following the upward march of benchmark Treasury yields, the 30-year fixed [USN:L1N45T0EH TEXT:"mortgage rate"] surged last week to a near three-year high, according to the Mortgage Bankers Association. Housing (.HGX) and homebuilders (.SPCOMHOME) slipped 2.3% and 2.9%, respectively. Chip stocks (.SOX) , which have soared over 80% so far this year, dropped 1.2%. [USN:L6N45S1CR TEXT:"SpaceX"] (SPCX.O) lost 2.5% following media reports that Elon Musk's aerospace firm was seeking $40 billion in financing to fund purchases of Nvidia chips. Next week, third-quarter reporting season is expected to begin in earnest with a spate of high-profile financial firms expected to post results. Investors are likely to scrutinize the extent to which massive expenditures on AI technology are beginning to show results, while also watching for clues regarding the health of the US consumer at a time of mounting inflationary pressures. Analysts currently expect year-on-year S&P 500 earnings growth of 30.6%, on aggregate, for the July-through-September period, according to LSEG. Declining issues outnumbered advancers by a 3.34-to-1 ratio on the NYSE. There were 115 new highs and 497 new lows on the NYSE. On the Nasdaq, 1,421 stocks rose and 3,371 fell as declining issues outnumbered advancers by a 2.37-to-1 ratio. The S&P 500 posted 9 new 52-week highs and 12 new lows while the Nasdaq Composite recorded 32 new highs and 250 new lows. Volume on US exchanges was 16.21 billion shares, compared with the 17.57 billion average for the full session over the last 20 trading days.

item.title: ルビオ米国務長官、ギリシャと安全保障上の脅威に共同対処と表明
item.description: [アテネ ７日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
[アテネ ７日 ロイター] - ルビオ米国務長官は７日、米国と「北大西洋条約機構（ＮＡＴＯ）の強力かつ模範的な同盟国」であるギリシャが法執行機関間で新たなテロ対策情報の共有を開始すると表明した。

アテネを公式訪問中のルビオ氏は、ギリシャは特に大規模な移民や人身売買による脅威にさらされていると述べた。

ギリシャのゲラペトリティス外相と並んで記者団に対し、「両国に共通するこれらの脅威と闘う取り組みの一環として、それぞれの法執行機関間のテロ対策情報共有を強化する共同安全保障プログラムを確立する新たな覚書を締結したことを、誇りを持って発表する」と語った。

ゲラペトリティス氏は、ホルムズ海峡で実行可能な和平プロセスが進めば、ギリシャは米国と協力し、同海峡での海上支援を提供する用意があると述べた。

ギルフォイル駐ギリシャ米大使が「米国は影響力を行使してギリシャ政府を弱体化させることができる」と脅したとの疑惑について米上院議員らが懸念を表明したことを巡っては、ルビオ氏は同大使を擁護。「ここにあるわれわれの大使館は素晴らしい仕事をしている。われわれの大使はこの地で力強い大使としての役割を果たしている」と述べた。

item.title: 独ポルシェ、販売減前提に事業再構築 最高価格帯に注力
item.description:
Rachel More Ilona Wissenbach
[ベルリン／フランクフルト ７日 ロイター] - ドイツの高...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
独ポルシェ、販売減前提に事業再構築　最高価格帯に注力 10/7 19:11 配信

写真はポルシェのロゴ。3月10日、ドイツ・ケルンで撮影。REUTERS/Jana Rodenbusch

Rachel More　Ilona Wissenbach

[ベルリン／フランクフルト ７日 ロイター] - ドイツの高級スポーツカーメーカー、ポルシェは７日、販売台数の減少を前提に事業を再構築すると明らかにした。需要が低迷する中でも、高級モデルへの注力で利益率の回復を目指す。

再建計画では、将来の損益分岐点となる販売台数を２０万台未満に引き下げる方針を示した。昨年の総納車台数２７万９４４９台を大幅に下回る水準となる。

ポルシェの世界納車台数は上場を果たした２０２２年から既に１０％近く減少した。中国での需要急減と米国の関税が打撃となっている。

南西部バイザッハの開発センターで開いた投資家向け説明会で、ミヒャエル・ライタース最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）は「９１１」などの高級スポーツカーに注力することで経営を立て直せると訴えた。年間販売の最高価格帯にある１万台について、販売価格の引き上げを目指す。

「世界で最も魅力的なスポーツカーメーカーとしてのポルシェの地位を強化したい」と述べ、ブランド価値の面でフェラーリやルイ・ヴィトンと肩を並べる存在に位置付けた。

＜２桁の利益率回復へ険しい道のり＞

ライタース氏は当面コスト削減に重点を置くと説明した。

ポルシェは今回の戦略で、グループ営業利益率の長期目標を１５％に設定した。おおむね５年以内を指す中期では、１０─１５％を目指す。利益率は上場した４年前の１０％台後半から、２５年には１．１％に急低下した。

発表を受けて株価は３．２％上昇した。

ライタース氏によると、現状では中期目標の下限を達成する見通しだ。それ以上の改善には、一段と踏み込んだ事業再編か「より好ましい事業環境」が必要になるという。

同氏は既存の人員削減策や管理職を４０％減らす計画に加え、開発費と販売費の削減で経営基盤を強化すると述べた。コスト削減に向け、同じフォルクスワーゲン（ＶＷ）傘下の高級車メーカー、アウディとの車台共用も拡大する方針だ。

ロイター 関連ニュース 焦点：空前のＡＩ投資、相応の経済効果実現へなお高いハードル コラム：円急伸で揺らぐキャリートレード、見つからない次の調達通貨 アングル：世界市場が当面向き合う6つのリスク、地政学や金融政策・ＡＩなど アングル：湾岸諸国、インフラ整備に重点投資　ホルムズ海峡封鎖で紛争耐性強化へ アングル：東京から欧州まで、猛暑で広がる男性の「短パン通勤」 最終更新: 10/7(水) 19:11 ロイター

item.title: 米有権者の過半数、政権・議会は「ＡＩのリスク深刻視せず」＝調査 - Reuters
item.description: 米有権者の過半数、政権・議会は「ＡＩのリスク深刻視せず」＝調査 Reuters

item.title: 米有権者の過半数、政権・議会は「ＡＩのリスク深刻視せず」＝調査
item.description:
Courtney Rozen Jason Lange
[ワシントン ７日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Courtney Rozen　Jason Lange

[ワシントン ７日 ロイター] - ロイター／イプソスの最新の世論調査によると、米有権者の過半数はトランプ政権と議会が人工知能（ＡＩ）のリスクを十分に深刻に受け止めていないと考えており、政府による新たな規制の策定を求めている。

調査は５日までの６日間実施。登録有権者３５２６人を含む成人４５０６人から回答を得た。

調査に回答した登録有権者の約５７％は、トランプ政権がＡＩのリスクを十分に深刻に受け止めていない、もしくは全く深刻に受け止めていないと答えた。共和党支持を自認する人でも３分の１が同様の見方を示した。議会のＡＩへの姿勢についても約５４％が同じ回答をした。

調査では、有権者の８４％がＡＩを米国の労働者にとって脅威と見なした。不法移民を米労働者に対する脅威だと回答したのは６０％だった。

ＡＩに対する政府の規制強化には党派を超えた過半数の有権者が賛成し、民主党支持者では８０％、共和党支持者でも６１％に上った。

ＡＩエージェントが暴走して企業のネットワークに不正侵入したとの報道や、ＡＩがいずれ人類の存続を脅かしかねないなどとする著名研究者の警告を受けて、ＡＩへの国民の関心は高まっており、１１月３日の中間選挙でも重要な争点となっている。

item.title: Aaron Sorkin on why he made another movie about Facebook, and how real life translates to film
item.description: LOS ANGELES, Oct 7 : Aaron Sorkin, the Oscar-winning screenwriter of "The Social Network," wasn't looking to make another movie about Facebook.Sorkin had been struggling to find an idea for a new project when he met Frances Haugen, a former Facebook employee and whistleblower whose disclosures raised concern
item.dc:creator: CNA
item.content:encoded:

Aaron Sorkin on why he made another movie about Facebook, and how real life translates to film

Director, writer, and producer Aaron Sorkin attends the Premiere of "The Social Reckoning,” in New York City, US, October 4, 2026. REUTERS/Angelina Katsanis

FAST

LOS ANGELES, Oct 7 : Aaron Sorkin, the Oscar-winning screenwriter of "The Social Network," wasn't looking to make another movie about Facebook. Sorkin had been struggling to find an idea for a new project when he met Frances Haugen, a former Facebook employee and whistleblower whose disclosures raised concerns about the impact on health, safety and global politics of the company's social media platforms. The story he crafted, told in the film "The Social Reckoning," will debut in theaters on Friday.  "I was looking for a good story, and after a period of about a year of just epic writer's block, of not being able to come up with any story, I met Frances Haugen, and suddenly a good story started to take shape in my head," Sorkin, who also directed the movie, said in an interview with Reuters. "The Social Network," released in 2010, told the origin story of Facebook, which has since changed its name to Meta, and starred Jesse Eisenberg as founder Mark Zuckerberg.

The new movie centers on Haugen and journalist Jeff Horwitz, who wrote a series for the Wall Street Journal called "The Facebook Files" that began in 2021 and was based largely on thousands of internal documents that she provided to him.  "It is a David and Goliath story, but there are two Davids," Sorkin said. "One is Frances. She picks up a rock and throws it at Facebook, and the other is print journalism. They pick up a rock and they throw it at tech." Horwitz, who later detailed the story in his 2023 book "Broken Code," now works as an investigative reporter for Reuters and remained on the Meta beat, earning a Pulitzer Prize in beat reporting this year with colleague Engen Tham for reports that exposed how Meta permitted its chatbots to engage in provocative behavior and earned billions of dollars in revenue from fraudulent ads. Sony Pictures bought the rights to his life story in connection to his previous Facebook reporting when employed by the Wall Street Journal. "The Social Reckoning" is a fictionalized account of events, and it does not draw upon Horwitz's reporting about Facebook, Instagram or Meta since he joined Reuters in 2025. The film chronicles Haugen's meetings with Horwitz starting in December 2020 and her reluctance to go public. Haugen eventually concludes the revelations will be more powerful with her name attached and decides to speak on the record. She also testifies before Congress to explain how she believed Facebook's algorithm was boosting divisive content in pursuit of profits. A Meta spokesperson declined to comment on the film. When Haugen testified, Facebook said the company disagreed with her characterization of how it operated. Zuckerberg defended the company in a Facebook post, writing that "the argument that we deliberately push content that makes people angry for profit is deeply illogical." In August, Meta agreed to pay up to $18 billion over the next decade to strictly limit how teenagers use Facebook and Instagram under a settlement with US states. The company denied wrongdoing and said ensuring that teens have a "safe and productive experience on our platforms" was an "absolute imperative" for the company. 'WHAT I DO IS A PAINTING' While Horwitz wasn't involved in the film's production and had no say over its content, he did meet with Sorkin and answered his questions about the reporting process and his relationship with Haugen. According to Horwitz, Sorkin said he would use some artistic license. "He told me that he thought he'd need to change some chronology and details to make the story he had in mind work," said Horwitz, who did not read the script until it was finished. "He also told me that he wanted to take some liberties with 'Movie Jeff,' who was sort of going to be a fictionalized, investigative reporter composite. It was definitely going to be an 'inspired by, not based on' situation." Sorkin said major facts of the story are accurate, although he had to create conversations and a timeline to make a compelling cinematic narrative. "People don't live their lives in a series of scenes that form a narrative by the end. People don't speak in dialogue. Those are things that screenwriters do," Sorkin said. "What you do as a journalist, that's a photograph," he added. "What I do is a painting." Zuckerberg, a supporting character in "The Social Reckoning," is played this time by "Succession" actor Jeremy Strong. Eisenberg declined the chance to reprise the role. "The Bear" star Jeremy Allen White portrays Horwitz, and Haugen is played by Mikey Madison, who won an Oscar for her role in "Anora."

Source: Reuters

item.title: Microsoft brings more AI to PCs as it challenges Apple
item.description: Microsoft unveiled on Wednesday an AI coding model that can run directly on personal computers and new security technology to prevent AI agents from accessing data without permission, challenging Apple's push to bring more AI into personal devices.
item.dc:creator: Stephen Nellis
item.content:encoded: Microsoft (MSFT.O) unveiled on Wednesday an AI coding model that can run directly on personal computers and new security technology to prevent AI agents from accessing data without permission, challenging Apple's (AAPL.O) push to bring more AI into personal devices. The software company also presented at the event in San Francisco a high-powered Surface laptop called Ultra powered by Nvidia's (NVDA.O) [USN:L6N42909E TEXT:"RTX Spark chips"]. Redmond, Washington-based Microsoft is seeking to turn Windows into a platform for AI agents to handle tasks such as writing computer code or tackling complex business projects on desktops and laptops. For Microsoft, the move represents a bet that some work that currently happens in its costly Azure cloud computing data centers can shift to high-powered Windows machines in businesses and homes, a market where the firm retains a stronghold — and where its customers foot the hardware bills. It is a market opportunity rival [USN:L6N45D0ZZ TEXT:"Apple is also chasing"] with new Mac computers. For Nvidia, cracking the Windows PC market could help it go after one of the last major markets dominated by Intel (INTC.O) and Advanced Micro Devices (AMD.O) . As a guardrail against increasingly autonomous AI agents that have created security risks, Microsoft said it was releasing Microsoft Execution Containers, a tool to prevent agents from accessing data and doing unauthorized tasks when running on a laptop or desktop machine. Anthropic, OpenAI and Nvidia will use the tools, said Pavan Davuluri, executive vice president for Windows and devices. “We needed to make the desktop the most secure place for agents to execute,” Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella said. Davuluri said new tools would let IT departments set rules for agents and the Windows operating system would enforce those rules on each employee’s machine. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, who joined Nadella on stage, said Microsoft’s new execution container technology, which goes by MXC for short, "is going to revolutionize how agents are built and deployed.” “Without it, (agents are) a complete nonstarter,” he said. Nvidia is [USN:L6N45K077 TEXT:"trying to prevent"] a repeat of the hack of AI hub Hugging Face, while Apple is looking to [USN:L6N45O14K TEXT:"tighten up the process"] for giving AI agents full access to a Mac computer's hard drive. AI MOVES TO THE PC Microsoft also unveiled AI models that previously required cloud access but can now run locally on high-powered Windows desktops and laptops, including Nvidia's open-source Nemotron model. Davuluri said a version of Chinese AI firm DeepSeek's V4 model can run on machines with at least 60 gigabytes of memory and outperform OpenAI's GPT-5 on some coding and reasoning tasks. Microsoft is taking a similar approach with its own Copilot AI assistant, splitting tasks between the cloud and individual laptops. “Copilot will still use the cloud for the hardest tasks, but for times when cost or privacy matter more, it can delegate down to local models that run directly on your computer,” said Microsoft’s Copilot chief Jacob Andreou. Davuluri also said Meta's (META.O) Muse personal assistant will come to Windows devices as a native app, using some of Microsoft’s new security tools, and that OpenClaw, the open-source AI agent system, can also work with those security tools. PRICE BARRIER One of the key challenges Microsoft and Nvidia face is the steep pricing of these devices after a memory-chip crunch drove up costs. The new Surface Laptop Ultra will start at $2,599 and rise to $5,899 for a model with a 20-core processor, 128 gigabytes of memory and one terabyte of storage. Apple's MacBook Pro with a 40-core graphics chip, 128 GB of memory and two TB of storage costs $6,700, although the machines are not directly comparable. Microsoft's entry-level Ultra costs more than Apple's $1,999 base MacBook Pro, but comes with 24 GB of memory compared with 16 GB on Apple's entry-level model. When Microsoft originally pitched the idea of running AI tasks on PCs two years ago to save costs, the laptops were mostly priced below $2,000, but Nvidia increased the price of an AI desktop machine called the DGX Spark by about 75% since its launch to $6,950 amid rising memory costs. Two years ago, "the software wasn't ready, but the hardware was. Now the software is ready and the hardware is too expensive to actually run it locally," said Anshel Sag, an analyst at Moor Insights & Strategy. "So it's becoming this thing where only the people who have the budget can really afford to run AI locally."

item.title: Most Republicans in tight midterm races distance themselves from Trump, Reuters review finds
item.description: Reuters reviewed voting records, public statements and campaign materials.
item.dc:creator: Nathan Layne, David Morgan
item.content:encoded: Two-thirds of Republican candidates in competitive US House and Senate races have broken with President Donald Trump on policy or played down ties to him, a Reuters review found, revealing a widespread effort to distance themselves from the president as his unpopularity threatens the party's hold on Congress. The review of voting records, public statements and campaign materials found candidates in 41 of 62 competitive congressional races seeking some distance from Trump ahead of the November 3 midterm elections . The candidates have largely criticized or diverged from Trump on individual issues rather than repudiated his broader agenda. The findings suggest an effort to attract independent voters while avoiding a direct break with their party leader. Policy differences were the most common point of divergence, appearing in 23 of the 62 races. In 12 contests, the split centered on the Iran conflict, with vulnerable Republicans either voting to curb Trump's war powers or calling publicly for an end to the fighting that has raised gas prices and squeezed household budgets. Data centers are among the issues dividing Trump and some Republican candidates. Reuters identified three candidates in competitive races who have criticized or sought to slow such projects despite the president's support for faster development. The shift is notable because Trump has spent the past decade remaking the Republican Party in his own image and has been swift to punish lawmakers and candidates who defied him through primary challenges, personal attacks or public pressure to fall into line. In response to questions about the Reuters findings, White House spokesman Davis Ingle pointed to the administration's accomplishments and said Trump was "the unequivocal leader, best messenger and unmatched motivator" for the party. While news organizations have highlighted individual cases of distancing, the Reuters review is the first to systematically measure the trend across competitive races that will decide whether Republicans retain control of either or both chambers of Congress. A new [USN:L6N45R10Y TEXT:"Reuters/Ipsos poll"] underscored the challenge facing Republicans: Trump's approval rating remained stuck at a career-low 32%, while registered voters favored Democrats over Republicans 44% to 37% ahead of the midterms. Among independents, Democrats led 37% to 21%. CREATING DISTANCE FROM TRUMP Reuters also found a broad effort to play down ties: A dozen candidates removed his name, image or endorsements from campaign websites, most after securing their party's nomination. Others acted in subtler ways, skipping his events or declining to say whether he should campaign on their behalf. Direct criticism was relatively rare, underscoring Trump's dominance of the Republican Party and the risks candidates face in openly challenging a president who still commands the loyalty of many ardent supporters. Candidates distancing themselves from an unpopular president before an election is not unusual. Democrats employed similar tactics in the 2014 and 2022 elections. While Reuters did not conduct a comparable review of competitive races in the 2018 midterms during Trump's first term, analysts said Trump has rarely faced such widespread pushback by vulnerable Republican candidates. "(Candidates) are reflecting voter attitudes in these races," said Republican strategist Ron Bonjean. "If (voters) are not with Trump, then they need to show a break." Privately, campaign advisers told Reuters that candidates needed to dial back ties to Trump to attract independent voters. Publicly, they dismissed criticism of the repositioning. BALANCING ACT Republican Senator Pete Ricketts, who faces a tough challenge from independent Dan Osborn in Nebraska, exemplifies the 11 candidates identified by Reuters who broke with Trump on one policy issue while backing him on everything else. The balancing act was on display this week when Ricketts, who criticized Trump's plan to expand beef imports, joined the president at a Nebraska rally. "President Trump, I have been fighting for you in Washington," Ricketts told the crowd. Mariannette Miller-Meeks, a Republican in one of the country's most competitive House races in Iowa, has also shown a growing willingness to break with the administration. She was among 12 candidates identified by Reuters who split with Trump on multiple issues, criticizing his beef-import policy and later voting to limit his war powers in Iran after previously opposing similar measures. Yet, less than two weeks after her war-powers vote, Miller-Meeks joined Trump at the White House to announce a major steel plant investment in Iowa. "It is a balancing act," said Republican consultant Jeanette Hoffman, adding that candidates are trying to capitalize on the administration’s successes while creating some distance from Trump because of “how toxic the Trump brand is at the moment.” SCRUBBING TRUMP REFERENCES As Republicans in competitive races seek to expand their appeal beyond Trump's core supporters, some candidates have begun dialing back public displays of loyalty to the president. Mike Beltran, a former Florida state representative running against Democratic US Representative Kathy Castor, is among candidates who have scrubbed prominent references to Trump from their campaign websites. In August, his homepage featured a photo of Trump and said he stood with the president, according to the Wayback Machine, an internet archive website. Now Beltran's homepage shows only him and his family and makes no mention of Trump. Beltran's campaign had no immediate response to a Reuters request for comment. Representative Mike Lawler of New York, facing one of the most competitive US House races, embodies the balancing act confronting many Republicans in battleground districts: staying close to Trump while demonstrating independence from him. Lawler has highlighted breaks with Trump on issues including temporary legal protections for Haitian immigrants and a Trump-backed proposal to restore Turkey's access to F-35 fighter jets. His campaign manager Ciro Riccardi said Lawler acts on behalf of his constituency regardless of a president's stance. Lawler acknowledged the disagreements in a speech to Trump supporters at the Republican midterm convention in September, saying, "The truth is that the president and I don't always agree. And that's OK."

item.title: AI companies run virtual drug trials, aim to improve success of human studies
item.description: Novartis’ experimental del-desiran for a rare type of muscular dystrophy was expected to be a winner, with the Swiss company's CEO predicting annual peak sales of $5 billion. When a late-stage trial missed its goal last month, shares fell 11%, erasing $30 billion in market value.
item.dc:creator: Deena Beasley
item.content:encoded: Novartis’ (NOVN.S) experimental del-desiran for a rare type of muscular dystrophy was expected to be a winner, with the Swiss company's CEO predicting annual peak sales of $5 billion. When a [USN:L8N45006F TEXT:"late-stage trial"] missed its goal last month, shares fell 11%, erasing $30 billion in market value. AI start-up BioinvestGPT was not surprised. In July, it ran a simulated trial to measure how virtual patients would respond to del-desiran and predicted an insignificant clinical benefit. It and other artificial intelligence companies say they are working with some drugmakers on virtual trials to boost the odds an experimental medicine will prove safe and effective when used by actual patients in an expensive traditional clinical trial. The global biopharmaceutical industry spends some $140 billion a year on human clinical testing, but only around 12% of drug candidates are approved by regulators — a rate that has changed little in decades. AI firms say simulations are being used to identify which pharmaceutical programs are worth moving forward and to assess the value of acquisition targets. As AI tools get better at flagging clinical risks, they say unexpected trial failures may become less frequent. Human clinical trials typically start with small Phase 1 studies primarily to gauge safety, followed by mid-stage Phase 2 and the large Phase 3 trials required by regulators that also assess efficacy. The process takes years, compared with a month or less for some AI simulations. "We shouldn't only ask how to run trials faster. We should ask how to run fewer trials that are going to fail," said Francisco Beca, chief medical officer at QuantHealth, an AI clinical trial simulation platform headquartered in Tel Aviv. Investment in AI drug discovery more than doubled to $8.4 billion in 2025 compared to 2023, according to a recent report from McKinsey . It said spending is currently focused where the technology works best today, particularly molecule design, rather than the industry's major bottlenecks, such as proving a drug will work as intended through lengthy trials. Pharma companies are "dipping their toes" into AI trial modeling, said McKinsey partner Alex Devereson. They are using different types of the technology, internally or with partners, to do things like assess drug candidates before committing capital to a program, he said. US health regulators last week announced a set of initiatives aimed at speeding drug trials. If successful, the program could help create a path for predictive AI to be used in clinical development, a federal health official said. FIVE OUT OF SIX CORRECT Copenhagen-based BioinvestGPT in July shared with Reuters its detailed analyses of the likely outcome of several high-profile drug trials before the results were known and has so far been correct in five of six. They include the negative result for del-desiran, success for Moderna (MRNA.O) and Merck's (MRK.N) [USN:L1N44F0SC TEXT:"melanoma vaccine"], a weak clinical benefit for AstraZeneca (AZN.L) and Ionis' (IONS.O) heart drug [USN:L6N43B0BH TEXT:"Wainua"], the first failed trial for Novo Nordisk's (NOVOb.CO) heart drug [USN:L4N43X1AC TEXT:"ziltivekimab"], and success for [USN:L4N45R0K6 TEXT:"Vaxcyte's"] (PCVX.O) pneumococcal vaccine. The fundamental goal of the pharma industry is proof of a superior clinical benefit compared to the standard of care, said Bragi Lovetrue, who co-founded BioinvestGPT with his wife Idonae Lovetrue in 2024. The AI platform uses DNA sequencing to simulate a human body matching the eligibility criteria for a specific clinical trial. A virtual trial is then done using a model of the test drug. "We can pinpoint the reason why a drug is effective and safe, and in many cases, why not," Lovetrue said. The simulations are not always right. The predictive AI forecast positive results for Novartis' [USN:L4N44W1D6 TEXT:"pelacarsen"], which lowers blood levels of a cholesterol-carrier called lipoprotein(a). Novartis in September said the drug did not cut the risk of a major heart attack or stroke in patients with a genetic risk factor in a late-stage trial. A subsequent analysis showed "we got the mechanism wrong," by not accounting for genetically set variations in the size of the lipoprotein, Lovetrue said. QuantHealth, which uses real-world data and AI to simulate patient-level responses to therapies, has published its simulations of ulcerative colitis and cholesterol drug trials. BIOGEN, TAKEDA TRIALS PREDICTED TO FAIL BioinvestGPT has done predictions for a wide range of trials. For anticipated trial results expected before year-end, the AI company predicts failure for two Phase 3 trials of Biogen's (BIIB.O) litifilimab in the most common type of lupus, as well as for Phase 2 studies of Japanese drugmaker Takeda's (4502.T) zasocitinib in Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis. The AI model shows that both drugs are "suboptimal" for those specific trial populations. Biogen's drug, which targets an immune cell receptor called BDCA2, is also being studied in a [USN:L4N45O11Z TEXT:"different type"] of lupus. Takeda filed recently for US approval of zasocitinib, which blocks an enzyme called tyrosine kinase 2, in plaque psoriasis and has a Phase 3 trial in psoriatic arthritis. Takeda research chief Andy Plump said TYK2 was identified as a target by analyzing human genetics, while machine learning was used to optimize and "polish" the structure of the daily pill. "I have immense confidence in this mechanism," Plump said. "I don't think we are near being able to use tools like AI to make definitive predictions." Diana Gallagher, Biogen's head of clinical development for multiple sclerosis, immunology and Alzheimer's, said the company uses "every tool available to us," including AI. She said only two biologic drugs have been approved for lupus and AI algorithms that rely on historical data could be prone to predicting a negative result. QuantHealth's Beca and other experts said human trials will always be necessary, but AI simulations can be valuable when assessing the potential of an experimental drug. "Is it still ethical in 2026 to expose patients to a trial that most likely will fail?" he said. "With the advancement of this (AI) technology, come 2027, 2028, or 2029, probably the answer is going to be that it no longer is."

Most US voters say Trump, Congress don't take AI risks seriously, Reuters/Ipsos poll finds

FAST

WASHINGTON, Oct 7 : Most US voters think President Donald Trump's administration and Congress are not taking the risks of AI seriously enough and want the government to write new regulations for the technology, according to a new Reuters/Ipsos poll. The six-day survey, which ended on Monday, showed that wide swaths of the electorate see AI as a major threat to American jobs, underscoring growing skepticism of the technology from voters across the political spectrum. The fast-advancing technology has become a matter of keen national interest amid reports of AI agents running amok and hacking into corporate computer networks, and warnings from prominent researchers that it could one day pose an existential threat to humanity. Noisy, power-hungry data centers that power AI also increasingly pose a nuisance when they pop up near neighborhoods while jacking up utility bills. Some 57 per cent of registered voters in the poll — including a third of self-identified Republicans — said the Trump administration has not taken AI risks seriously enough or at all. Some 54 per cent said the same about Congress.

Artificial intelligence has become a significant campaign issue ahead of the November 3 midterm elections when control of Congress is up for grabs. Some 62 per cent of voters in the poll said the technology could get out of control and risk the future of humankind, roughly the same share of voters with that view in a Reuters/Ipsos poll from August of last year.  Trump has repeatedly voiced unhesitating support for AI and the construction of data centers, arguing they are vital to US competitiveness even as bipartisan criticism of the technology grows. He often says the US tech industry will fall behind its Chinese counterparts when asked why his government hasn't set limits on the technology's use and development, a point that AI safety advocates say is misguided.  "That's an important concern but it's not top of mind for most Americans, nor should it be," said Daniel Kokotajlo, a former OpenAI staffer who quit in 2024 because he believed the company wasn't behaving responsibly. The more pressing concern is that AI could cost people their jobs or threaten human health and safety, he said. In a statement to Reuters about the president's handling of AI, a White House official pointed to Trump's new task force, which he said is in charge of ensuring that "America continues to lead the world" on the technology. "The Trump administration’s priority is to ensure there is a booming economy so that workers have many opportunities and experience limited volatility from any short-term disruptions," the official said when asked about voters' AI-related employment fears. LITTLE FEDERAL ACTION While high-profile leaders ranging from US Senator Bernie Sanders — a democratic socialist who caucuses with Democrats — to Steve Bannon — a hard right ally of President Donald Trump — have called for federal action, little has come so far. Trump last week said executives from the six leading AI developers agreed to a set of voluntary safety principles, including working with "independent auditors" to assess whether AI systems are working as their designers intended. The safety agreement with the companies — Nvidia, SpaceX, OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta and Alphabet’s Google — includes no stated consequences if a company chooses not to comply. Congress has so far failed to agree on legislation that would set guardrails on the technology, and lawmakers are expected to be away from Washington until after the midterms.  The new Reuters/Ipsos poll found 84 per cent of voters saw AI as a threat to American workers. By comparison, only 60 per cent saw illegal immigration as a threat to American workers, while 74 per cent viewed competition from foreign workers that way and 73 per cent said the same of large corporations. A bipartisan majority of voters - including 80 per cent of Democrats and 61 per cent of Republicans - said they supported stricter government regulation on AI. Many voters also oppose building the data centers that power AI, which has become a pressing issue in congressional and statewide races across the country as candidates from both parties urge a pause in the current construction boom. Fifty-six percent of voters in the Reuters/Ipsos poll back limits on building data centers, including 69 per cent of Democrats, 55 per cent of independents and 43 per cent of Republicans.  The poll also found growing unease with the ways that AI could be used in warfare. Some 57 per cent of voters think the US government should not use AI to determine the target of a military strike, up from 49 per cent in a Reuters/Ipsos poll conducted in August 2025. The Reuters/Ipsos poll, which was conducted online and nationwide, gathered responses from 4,506 US adults, including 3,526 registered voters. The survey has a margin of error of 2 per centage points.

Source: Reuters

item.title: US bonds selloff eases, yields off highs, after strong 10-year note auction
item.description: US Treasuries rose in afternoon trading on Wednesday, with yields backing away from their highs as oil prices fell and a strong $39 billion auction of 10-year notes reassured investors that demand for long-term government debt remained intact despite recent market volatility.
item.dc:creator: Gertrude Chavez-Dreyfuss
item.content:encoded: US Treasuries rose in afternoon trading on Wednesday, with yields backing away from their highs as oil prices fell and a strong $39 billion auction of 10-year notes reassured investors that demand for long-term government debt remained intact despite recent market volatility. US government debt earlier came under renewed selling pressure, driving yields on the benchmark 10-year note and 30-year bond to fresh 24-year highs as oil prices jumped above $100. That re-ignited worries that inflation may prove more stubborn than expected. Rising yields mean Treasury debt prices were higher. A strong $39 billion sale of 10-year notes sparked buying across the Treasury market, analysts said. Some investors had feared weak demand given persistent bearish sentiment toward longer-dated Treasuries in recent months, driven in part by renewed concerns over rising fiscal deficits. "It was a good auction given how much the 10-year has sold off, and it's good to see buyers step in," said Vinny Bleau, director of fixed income research at Raymond James in Memphis. "You can be afraid of it (the selloff), or you can take advantage of it." The drop in oil prices also helped yields drift lower from their highs after the International Energy Agency [USN:L6N45T0GQ TEXT:"agreed to speed up"] a release of oil stocks and prioritize diesel in a bid to curb record high fuel prices. Brent crude fell 0.5% to $100.09 per barrel, while US crude slid 1.1% to $88.32 per barrel. In afternoon trading, the benchmark 10-year yield was up 1.3 basis points (bps) to 5.284% after hitting a 24-year peak of 5.364% earlier. US 30-year yields also touched a 24-year high and were last 2.8 bps higher at 5.669% . On the shorter end of the curve, US 2-year yields, which reflect interest rate expectations, were down 2.3 bps at 4.768% . SPACEX FACTOR US debt was also earlier undermined by reports that Elon Musk's SpaceX (SPCX.O) , a rockets-to-AI firm, was [USN:L6N45S1CR TEXT:"seeking $40 billion in financing"] to fund purchases of Nvidia chips. The Financial Times reported that SpaceX is looking to raise about $10 billion in bank loans and $30 billion in investment-grade debt for the chip order. If SpaceX enters the investment-grade bond market, it could revive concerns that large-scale corporate borrowing is competing with long-dated US Treasuries for investor capital, analysts said. "The amount of demand of private sector borrowing, particularly for long paper ... has grown so significantly that it has created this crowding-out effect or competition for capital," said Thomas Urano, co-chief investment officer at Sage Advisory in Austin. The 10-year Treasury auction, meanwhile, went down smoothly, pricing at [USN:AQN2MN6IG TEXT:"5.3%"], lower than the expected rate at the bid deadline, suggesting that investors did not need a premium to take down the benchmark debt. The bid-to-cover ratio, a measure of demand, was 2.77, above the six-auction average of 2.54. Primary dealers were left with just 2.5% of the offering, their smallest share since the aftermath of the global financial crisis, suggesting investor demand was strong enough that dealers were not required to absorb much of the issue. 'CALMED THE NERVES' "The strong stop through and high end-user demand may have calmed the nerves of some investors thinking that there would be no demand given the rise in yields," said Gennadiy Goldberg, head of US rates strategy at TD Securities. "On the contrary, we think higher yields are prompting investors to dip their toes even as they worry about recent volatility." Minutes of the Federal Reserve's September meeting were also released on Wednesday, [USN:L6N45T0TQ TEXT:"with policymakers divided"] over the rationale for raising interest rates. "Some participants" saw a hike as needed to keep the impact of energy and other price shocks at bay, but a more hawkish core viewed it as necessary to guard against emerging demand-driven inflation, the minutes showed. Elsewhere in the Treasury market, the yield curve steepened on Wednesday with the spread between two-year and 10-year yields widening to 52.2 bps from 48.1 bps. The curve hit 53.7 bps, its steepest level since mid-August after long-dated yields rose more sharply than shorter-dated ones, a move known as a bear steepener. A bear steepener reflects a pickup in inflation expectations.

item.description:
Andrea Shalal

item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
債務に苦しむ開発途上国支援へ構想提案、ＩＭＦ総会控え専門家ら 10/7 19:00 配信

写真は米ドルと中国人民元の紙幣。2023年1月撮影。REUTERS/Dado Ruvic

Andrea Shalal

[ワシントン ７日 ロイター] - ロックフェラー財団などの専門家らは７日、多額の債務を抱える開発途上国が経済成長を図り、必要な投資を行い、民間資本を活用できるよう、新たな資金へのアクセスを支援するイニシアチブ「成長・投資リセット」を提案した。

国際通貨基金（ＩＭＦ）、世界銀行、２国間公的債権者、民間貸し手らの取り組みを調整することで、低所得国が深刻な債務危機に陥るのを防ぐことを目的としているという。

必要な政治的合意を確保し、英国が議長国を務める来年の主要２０カ国・地域（Ｇ２０） の下で取り組みを前進させることを目指す。論文執筆者らは「開発途上国は不可欠な投資を圧迫する前例のない利払い負担に苦しんでいる。緊急の対策が講じられなければ、状況はさらに悪化するだろう」と述べた。

執筆者の１人によると、開発途上国における利払い額は平均して歳入の１０％を超えており、１０カ国ではその額が公共投資を上回っている。債務水準が持続可能な約４０カ国がこのイニシアチブの適用対象となるが、一部の国では依然として債務再編が必要になるという。

今回の提案は来週バンコクで開催されるＩＭＦ・世界銀行年次総会を控えて行われた。

item.description: [７日 ロイター] - ドイツの高級車メーカー、メルセデス・ベンツは７日、中国市場の厳しい状況により、主力事業であ...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
メルセデス・ベンツ、第3四半期自動車販売8％減　中国で不振 10/7 18:59 配信

写真はモスクワのディーラーに掲げられたメルセデス・ベンツのロゴ。2025年12月撮影。REUTERS/Ramil Sitdikov

[７日 ロイター] - ドイツの高級車メーカー、メルセデス・ベンツは７日、中国市場の厳しい状況により、主力事業である乗用車部門の第３・四半期の販売台数が前年同期比８％減となり、減少傾向が続いたと発表した。

• 第３・四半期の自動車販売台数は４０万７２００台。

• 中国市場では、前年同期比３１％減の８万６８００台となった。

• ハイエンドセグメントの販売台数は、中国における市場環境の悪化や継続中のモデルチェンジの影響を受け、２１％減の５万３９００台となった。

• 一方、米国では乗用車販売台数が６％増、欧州では５％増となった。

• 乗用車やバンを含むグループ全体のバッテリー式電気自動車（ＥＶ）の販売台数は、５２％増の７万８１００台となった。

item.description: BERLIN, Oct 7 : Tesla CEO Elon Musk on Wednesday welcomed Germany's backing for the US automaker's driver-assistance software system, as he seeks Europe-wide approval for the technology that traffic-safety researchers have warned carries inflated safety claims. "Danke schoen," wrote Musk on his social media
item.dc:creator: CNA
item.content:encoded:
Advertisement

Musk welcomes German backing for Tesla driver assistance tech as group chases EU approval

FILE PHOTO: Tesla enthusiast Kees Roelandschap drives around hands-free with his electric car, several days after Dutch regulators approved the use of Tesla's self-driving software, in Amsterdam, Netherlands, April 17, 2026. REUTERS/Bart Biesemans/File Photo

FILE PHOTO: The logo of Tesla is seen on a Tesla Model Y during Tesla Inc.'s official launch in Bogota, Colombia, November 20, 2025. REUTERS/Luisa Gonzalez/File Photo

FILE PHOTO: Tesla CEO Elon Musk attends the Saudi-U.S. Investment Forum, in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, May 13, 2025. REUTERS/Hamad I Mohammed/File Photo

FAST

BERLIN, Oct 7 : Tesla CEO Elon Musk on Wednesday welcomed Germany's backing for the US automaker's driver-assistance software system, as he seeks Europe-wide approval for the technology that traffic-safety researchers have warned carries inflated safety claims. "Danke schoen," wrote Musk on his social media platform X about German Transport Minister Steffen Bilger pushing for approval of the "Full Self-Driving" technology across Europe. Bilger said in a statement on Tuesday that he is advocating for prompt EU approval after discussing numerous technical details, as well as liability issues, with Tesla last month. A Reuters report published Wednesday detailed how Tesla has mounted a pressure campaign to win FSD approval in the EU by casting safety regulators as feckless bureaucrats blocking its life-saving technology. Tesla has pushed regulators directly to reduce the rigour of safety reviews, submitted its own research making bold crash-reduction claims, and used social media to mobilize Tesla enthusiasts to demand speedy approvals.

But Tesla’s lobbying is built on faulty company safety research that can’t support the company’s safety claims to officials or the public, according to seven traffic-safety researchers who examined its methodology for Reuters. The company’s European research doesn’t examine crash rates or traffic deaths at all, instead using certain driving behaviours, such as hard braking or horn-honking, as a proxy. As part of its discussions with Tesla, Germany agreed with the company that the system may slightly exceed the maximum speed limit by up to 10 per cent – an approach Germany will also support within the European approval process, where speeding has become one of the main points of contention. Safety advocates and some regulators argue Tesla's use of a speed-offset function, which allows the system to drive above the posted limit, should be removed before approval is granted. Bilger added that Tesla has also offered to rename the system "Tesla Assisted Driving" to address concerns that the name is somewhat misleading. The system offers assistance to drivers, but is not fully autonomous. "My goal is for Tesla drivers to be able to enjoy the benefits of 'assisted driving' throughout the EU without delay," said Bilger. TESLA LOBBYING HARD FOR EU APPROVAL Germany is the latest in a handful of European countries, including the Netherlands and Belgium, to throw their support behind the technology. However, several EU countries, including Sweden and France, have expressed concerns about FSD exceeding speed limits, and an EU vote expected for October has been pushed back to at least December while some countries do additional tests. The Europe-specific version of the system approved by Dutch regulators earlier this year excluded some features available in the US, including a so-called 'Mad Max' setting, but retained a function that can lift the vehicle's maximum speed to as much as 50 per cent above the detected speed limit. Tesla, whose first European factory was built outside Berlin, has called FSD approval key to boosting sales in Europe, where it is seeking to regain market share amid growing competition from Chinese electric-vehicle makers.

Source: Reuters

item.description: ［香港 ７日 ロイター］ - 香港株式市場は下落した。アジア市場全般の軟調な地合いを受けた流れで、原油価格が上昇する...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
中国・香港株式市場・大引け＝香港下落、ＡＩ・バイオテク株に売り 10/7 18:25 配信

［香港　７日　ロイター］ - 香港株式市場は下落した。アジア市場全般の軟調な地合いを受けた流れで、原油価格が上昇する中、人工知能（ＡＩ）関連株とバイオテクノロジー株が下げを主導した。

ハンセン指数は０．６％安、ハンセン中国株指数も０．６％安で引けた。

ハンセンテック指数は０．７％下げた。

テンプルトン・グローバル・インベストメンツのリサーチ責任者、バッセル・カトゥン氏はリポートで「政策支援にもかかわらず中国市場は低調にとどまった。消費需要の弱さと製造業指標のまちまちな結果が、テクノロジー分野への選別的な関心を打ち消した」と述べた。

この日は香港上場の中国ＡＩ・テック企業が売り圧力にさらされた。

ＡＩ開発企業のミニマックスが４％下落し、半導体メーカーの華虹半導体とテクノロジー大手アリババはそれぞれ３％下げた。

バイオテクノロジー株は前営業日の急伸を受けて２．８％下落した。

景気活動の鈍化を背景に、香港の９月のＳ＆Ｐ購買担当者景気指数（ＰＭＩ）は０．３ポイント低下して４９．２となり、市場心理の弱さに拍車をかけた。同指数は好不況の分かれ目となる５０を２カ月連続で下回った。

中国本土の金融市場は国慶節（建国記念日）の連休で１０月１日から７日まで休場で、取引は１０月８日に再開する。

item.title: ＷＨＯ、ロシアに詳細な情報提供求める ペスト研究所職員死亡巡り
item.description: [７日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
[７日 ロイター] - 世界保健機関（ＷＨＯ）は７日、シベリアのペスト研究所職員が死亡した原因について、ロシアにさらなる情報の提供を要請したと発表し、潜在的な健康リスクを明確に把握するためには透明性が不可欠だと述べた。

テドロス事務局長はＸを通じ、「重度の肺炎の原因、公衆衛生措置のきっかけとなった病原体、および原因不明の肺炎を患った２人目の職員に関するメディア報道を明らかにするため、さらなる情報を要請した」と明らかにした。

一部の西側メディアは具体的に明かされていない「ロシアメディア」を引用し、シベリアで２人目の死者が出ており、その死因はペストだと報道。ロイターはロシアメディアにそのような報道を見いだすことができておらず、シベリアで２人目の死者が出たという証拠も確認できなかった。

ロシア保健当局は、研究所職員が肺炎にかかって死亡したと発表しているが、その原因については公に説明していない。肺炎には、ペストを含め、さまざまな原因が考えられる。

item.title: イラク、通貨ディナールを14.5％切り下げ 石油収入減に対応か
item.description:
Tala Ramadan Ahmed Rasheed
[７日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Tala Ramadan　Ahmed Rasheed

[７日 ロイター] - イラク内閣は通貨ディナールの新たな為替レート体系を承認した。１ドル＝１５２０ディナールに設定し、従来の公定レートから約１４．５％切り下げた。イラン戦争で石油販売に支障が生じたことへの対応とみられる。

通貨切り下げは６日に採択され、７日に発効した。財務省の買い入れレートは１ドル＝１５００ディナール、銀行とノンバンク金融機関が最終利用者に売却する際のレートは同１５１０ディナールとした。

イラクのアナリスト、モハメド・アルサファル氏は「今回のディナール切り下げは基本的に、イラン戦争と輸出の混乱による石油収入への打撃に対する財政的な対応だ」と述べた。「政府は石油収入１ドル当たりで得られるディナールを増やせる一方、輸入コストが上がり、家計の購買力は低下する」と指摘した。

item.description:
Hiroko Hamada
［東京 ７日 ロイター］ - 日本取引所グループのＪＰＸ総研は７日、ＴＯＰＩＸ改革の第２段...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
次期ＴＯＰＩＸに35銘柄採用、日本マクドナルドＨＤなど　除外候補は683銘柄 10/7 18:13 配信

東証。4月撮影。REUTERS/Issei Kato

Hiroko Hamada

［東京　７日　ロイター］ - 日本取引所グループのＪＰＸ総研は７日、ＴＯＰＩＸ改革の第２段階となる見直しで、新たに３５銘柄を採用すると発表した。既存銘柄のうち、基準未達となった移行措置銘柄は６８３銘柄。次期ＴＯＰＩＸの構成銘柄（２０２８年７月末）は９８６銘柄となる見込み。

新規では、日本マクドナルドホールディングス、フェローテック、ワークマン、タイミー、トライアルホールディングスなどが採用された。プライム市場以外では、スタンダードから２３銘柄、グロースから１２銘柄が選定された。

移行措置銘柄には、パソナグループ、三菱総合研究所、コジマ、学研ホールディングス、ブックオフグループホールディングス、テレビ東京ホールディングスなどが入った。

定期入れ替えはプライム、スタンダード、グロースの全市場を対象に、年間売買代金回転率と浮動株時価総額の累積比率という流動性基準をもとに年１回、１０月末に実施される。継続基準を満たさなかった移行措置銘柄は、四半期ごとに８段階でウエートを低減する。移行措置銘柄の再評価は２０２７年１０月に実施される予定で、２７年１０月時点で継続基準を満たした場合は段階的ウエート低減を停止する。２回目の定期入替は２８年１０月。

item.content:encoded:
ドイツ輸出、今年の伸び率見通しを1％に上方修正＝業界団体 10/7 18:09 配信

写真は独ブレーマーハーフェンのコンテナターミナル。2025年8月撮影。REUTERS/Leon Kuegeler

[ベルリン ７日 ロイター] - ドイツ卸売・貿易連盟（ＢＧＡ）は７日、２０２６年の輸出伸び率見通しを０．６％から１％に上方修正した。欧州での堅調な需要に支えられて予想外に好調だった上半期を受けた。

ＢＧＡによると、上半期の輸出総額は約８１８０億ユーロ（９１６０億ドル）で前年同期比３．９％増となり、輸入は約７１２０億ユーロで４．７％増加した。

通年の輸入伸び率見通しは３％に据え置いた。

ＢＧＡは「ドイツの対外貿易は安定しつつあるが、好転にはまだ程遠い」と述べ、米国および中国への輸出が低迷していることに言及。サプライチェーン（供給網）と市場の多様化を図るとともに、欧州企業の中国市場へのアクセスを改善するよう求めた。

「リスク軽減はデカップリングを意味してはならず、戦略的自立は自給自足を意味してはならない」と述べた。

item.description:

• 調査対象となったファミリーオフィスのうち、３７％が金利と利回りの上昇を世界経済成長にとって最大のリスクと回答し、次いでインフレが２３％、ＡＩ（人工知能）関連リスクが１７％と続いた。
• 回答者の７３％が、今後１２カ月間で最も安定した地政学的地域としてアジアを挙げ、次いで米国が１４％、英国および欧州が６％、ラテンアメリカが４％、中東が２％となった。

[シンガポール ７日 ロイター] - ７日に発表されたドイツ銀行の調査によると、世界の富裕層は金利と利回りの上昇を世界経済の成長に対する最大の脅威と見なしている一方で、その大多数は今後１２カ月間でアジアが最も安定した地政学的地域になると予想している。

詳細は以下の通り。

• 調査はシンガポールで開催された同行の「エマージング・マーケッツ・ファミリーオフィス・フォーラム２０２６」において実施され、約２００のファミリーオフィスや富裕層が参加した。

• 調査対象となったファミリーオフィスのうち、３７％が金利と利回りの上昇を世界経済成長にとって最大のリスクと回答し、次いでインフレが２３％、ＡＩ（人工知能）関連リスクが１７％と続いた。

• 回答者の７３％が、今後１２カ月間で最も安定した地政学的地域としてアジアを挙げ、次いで米国が１４％、英国および欧州が６％、ラテンアメリカが４％、中東が２％となった。
